learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the electoral process, the crucial role of the Election Commission, and how voting forms the backbone of a democracy!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In a large democracy, not everyone can sit together to make decisions. Elections allow citizens to choose representatives who will make laws and govern on their behalf.
The country is divided into smaller geographic areas called constituencies. Voters in each area elect one representative. For the Lok Sabha, India has 543 constituencies.
Officially called the Electoral Roll. It is a list of all citizens aged 18 and above who are eligible to vote. It ensures the principle of Universal Adult Franchise.
A period where candidates try to persuade voters to vote for them. They hold rallies, make promises through a 'Manifesto', and debate issues. It ends 48 hours before polling.
In India, elections are conducted by an independent and powerful body called the Election Commission. It ensures elections are free and fair, and enforces the Model Code of Conduct.

fun_activity.title: 📢 Write a Manifesto
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are running for Class President. Write down three big promises (Manifesto) you will make to your classmates to win their votes!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the difference between General Elections (held for all seats every 5 years) and By-elections (held for one seat due to death or resignation).
📌 Be able to explain the powers of the Election Commission (e.g., implementing the code of conduct, punishing candidates).
📌 'Universal Adult Franchise' means all adult citizens (18+) have the right to vote, regardless of caste, religion, or gender.
quick_recap: ⭐ India has a multi-party system where many parties compete for power.
⭐ Some constituencies are 'Reserved' for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) to ensure their fair representation.
⭐ EVMs (Electronic Voting Machines) are used to record votes safely and count them quickly.
